sampling_model.design: Independent repeated complete scenes from prespecified source skeletons; one representative node per supported type--context row is fixed before sampling.
sampling_model.units: Finite source scenes with the relational skeletons in \(Rsrc\).
sampling_model.treatment: The target intervention \(\operatorname{do}(a)\) is fixed; inferential randomness comes from sampled source scenes, not from target intervention assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Population transfer uses only positive source parent contexts for target-relevant rows other than \(rstar\). For confidence boxes, each prespecified representative source-node parent context is separately required to have positive probability; \(rstar\) remains unrestricted on \([0,1]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For the prespecified positive-probability representative contexts, construct simultaneous rational coordinate boxes for supported categorical rows, intersect them with row simplices, choose rational \(etahat\), and use the labeled occurrence radius \(\delta\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The complete relational identification procedure returns an identifying expression or \(\mathsf{FAIL}\), and neural extrema agree exactly when the query is identified.
Canonical finite SCMs reduce arbitrary discrete counterfactual sharp bounds to a polynomial program.
Polynomial programming yields numerical sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds and confidence-region relaxations for discrete causal queries.
Untrusted algebraic root certificates can be checked skeptically by verified univariate CAD and Sturm--Tarski computations.
Root counting and interval subdivision decide univariate polynomial relation systems soundly and completely in PVS.
Exact real-root isolation with multiplicities and nonsquare-free inputs has explicit polynomial bit-complexity bounds.
Unnested univariate parametric Markov-chain model checking is polynomial-time after the parametric model is explicit.
A response-signature LP gives tight causal-order bounds and constructs attaining SCMs.

body.tldr: A finite Markovian relational SCM with exactly one target-relevant binary row unsupported by positive source parent contexts has a sharp interventional range equal to the exact image of one rational polynomial. A fixed skeptical certificate binds the complete schema, graphs, source tables, target query, context incidence, dense polynomial, and serialized endpoint groundings; its checker replays the relational target factorization before certifying exhaustive derivative roots, exact algebraic endpoints, and source-compatible finite-noise endpoint RSCMs, with size and checking cost polynomial in the complete explicit encoding. The interval strictly refines Ejaz and Bareinboim only when their complete procedure actually returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) and \(F\) is nonconstant; a constant \(F\) gives the same point-identification conclusion. Supported-row confidence boxes use a separate sampling-positivity condition and yield a conservative occurrence-coupled enclosure. The first open extension is width-sensitive proof-carrying production from succinct groundings.

project_justification.gap: When the complete relational identification procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\), it does not report the exact compatible causal range; general discrete-SCM bounding and univariate algebra do not jointly certify the relational derivation of the objective, source reproduction, algebraic extrema, and endpoint models.
project_justification.niche: Exactly one unsupported binary row collapses a high-dimensional causal program to a one-dimensional polynomial image without making endpoint attainment or causal certificate semantics automatic.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the sharp image theorem, serializes common finite-noise endpoint RSCMs, and supplies a sound, complete certificate that binds and replays the complete fixed relational instance with polynomial size and checking cost, followed by an explicitly conservative sampling enclosure under separately stated representative-context positivity.

body.related_work: Ejaz and Bareinboim define RSCMs, give the relevant target-context support result, and supply a complete identification procedure with a neural criterion. The only strict comparator promise is conditional: when that complete procedure actually returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) and \(F\) is nonconstant, the sharp interval is more informative; a missing sufficient support condition alone is not treated as failure, and constant \(F\) yields equal point identification. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide the canonical finite-SCM equivalence and sharp polynomial-program construction that informs the causal completeness argument. Duarte et al. provide general numerical polynomial bounds and confidence-constraint relaxation; the present exact univariate solver and occurrence-coupling enclosure are different specializations, not claimed improvements to their general algorithm. Kline and Tamer's 2023 review supplies the current partial-identification framing of identified-set characterization and set coverage. Li, Passmore, and Paulson supply the skeptical producer--checker architecture, while Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle and Tsigaridas and Emiris supply sound root-counting and multiplicity-aware isolation primitives. Hutschenreiter, Baier, and Klein show that explicit univariate parametric model checking is polynomial for unnested formulas, which marks the occupied algebraic core and motivates width-sensitive production from succinct groundings. Rossetto and Antonucci construct attaining SCMs for order-based LP bounds over a broader nonrelational class; their witnesses do not enforce the present type-shared independent-ground-noise semantics.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The fixed certificate transaction includes the complete explicit relational instance, context incidence, dense coefficient list, and a replayable target-factorization derivation. Producing this explicit input from a succinct relational description by exhaustive target-assignment expansion may be exponential. The confidence result does not compute the exact multivariate projection over supported-row boxes; interior nuisance optima and a maximum-clique encoding rule out a generic vertex-enumeration shortcut.
body.honest_scope: The interval identity and breakpoint witness architecture are mathematically concrete but remain to be proved in the typed core. The load-bearing work is the universal soundness, completeness, size, and checking theorem for a grammar that binds the complete fixed relational instance, verifies membership in \(Mone\), and replays the factorization yielding \(F\), followed by the independent cubic producer--checker transaction. General succinct compilation, several unsupported rows, conditional postintervention queries, efficient confidence width, and empirical usefulness beyond the documented N3 example remain open. Failure of a sufficient support condition does not itself imply that the complete Ejaz--Bareinboim procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\). As sanity reductions, \(F(q)=q\) gives the logical range \([0,1]\), while constant \(F\) gives a singleton and agrees with point identification.
